screen.definition: The surface on which a film image is displayed.
screen.exampleUsage: The film image appeared on the screen.

auditorium.definition: The audience room in a cinema.
auditorium.exampleUsage: Visitors entered the auditorium before the screening.

lobby.definition: A large entrance or reception room or area.
lobby.exampleUsage: They met in the lobby near the ticket facility.

box-office.definition: The place where cinema or event tickets are sold or collected.
box-office.exampleUsage: The visitor collected tickets at the box office.

concession-stand.definition: A counter where snacks and drinks are sold at a cinema, stadium, or event venue.
concession-stand.exampleUsage: The concession stand sells snacks and drinks.

hallway.definition: An interior passage or corridor onto which rooms open.
hallway.exampleUsage: The hallway connects the lobby to the audience rooms.

emergency-exit.definition: A clearly marked doorway or route allows people to evacuate quickly when fire, collapse, or another serious threat occurs.
emergency-exit.exampleUsage: The venue identified the emergency exit.

projection-room.definition: A room containing equipment used to project a film or digital image onto a cinema screen.
projection-room.exampleUsage: The projection room contains film-presentation equipment.

restroom.definition: A public room containing toilets and washing facilities.
restroom.exampleUsage: The visitor asked for the restroom.

parking-lot.definition: An area with marked spaces where vehicles can be parked.
parking-lot.exampleUsage: The parking lot contains marked vehicle spaces.

seat.definition: Any support where you can sit (especially the part of a chair or bench etc. on which you sit).
seat.exampleUsage: The visitor found the booked seat.

row.definition: An arrangement of objects or people side by side in a line.
row.exampleUsage: The ticket identifies the seating row.

aisle.definition: Passageway between seating areas as in an auditorium or passenger vehicle or between areas of shelves of goods as in stores.
aisle.exampleUsage: The aisle provides a passage between the seats.

armrest.definition: A support beside a seat on which a person rests an arm.
armrest.exampleUsage: The armrest supports the seated visitor's arm.

cup-holder.definition: A small holder designed to keep a cup or bottle upright.
cup-holder.exampleUsage: The cup holder keeps the drink container upright.

3d-glasses.definition: Glasses worn to make a 3D film appear to have depth.
3d-glasses.exampleUsage: The visitor wore 3D glasses for the compatible screening.

recliner.definition: An armchair whose back can be lowered and foot can be raised to allow the sitter to recline in it.
recliner.exampleUsage: The recliner has an adjustable back.

balcony.definition: An upper floor projecting from the rear over the main floor in an auditorium.
balcony.exampleUsage: The balcony provides an upper seating area.

front-row.definition: Seats nearest the stage, podium, or front of a room form the front row.
front-row.exampleUsage: The front row is nearest the screen in this auditorium.

back-row.definition: The final row of seats farthest from the front or screen.
back-row.exampleUsage: The back row is farthest from the screen.

popcorn.definition: Small pieces of corn heated until they burst into white pieces.
popcorn.exampleUsage: The visitor bought popcorn at the snack counter.

soda.definition: A sweet drink containing carbonated water and flavoring.
soda.exampleUsage: The counter served a carbonated soda.

nachos.definition: Tortilla chips commonly served with cheese and other toppings.
nachos.exampleUsage: The nachos were served with cheese and other toppings.

candy.definition: A rich sweet made of flavored sugar and often combined with fruit or nuts.
candy.exampleUsage: The visitor selected a packet of candy.

hot-dog.definition: A cooked sausage, often served in a long split bread roll.
hot-dog.exampleUsage: The counter served a hot dog in a bread roll.

ice-cream.definition: A frozen sweet dessert commonly made with dairy ingredients or suitable alternatives.
ice-cream.exampleUsage: The visitor ordered ice cream as a frozen dessert.

pretzel.definition: A twisted baked snack covered with salt.
pretzel.exampleUsage: The pretzel was sold as a baked snack.

slushie.definition: A thick cold drink made from crushed ice mixed with flavored liquid.
slushie.exampleUsage: The slushie contains crushed ice and flavored liquid.

water-bottle.definition: A container used for carrying drinking water.
water-bottle.exampleUsage: The water bottle holds drinking water.

combo-meal.definition: A set meal sold as one package, usually combining a main item with a side or drink.
combo-meal.exampleUsage: The combo meal bundles the selected food and drink.

movie.definition: A form of entertainment that enacts a story by sound and a sequence of images giving the illusion of continuous movement.
movie.exampleUsage: The movie tells its story through moving images and sound.

trailer.definition: A promotional preview of a film.
trailer.exampleUsage: The trailer gives a promotional preview of the film.

credits.definition: The list of people and organizations that helped make a film.
credits.exampleUsage: The credits list contributors to the film.

director.definition: The person guiding a film’s artistic interpretation and performance.
director.exampleUsage: The director guided the film's interpretation and performances.

actor.definition: A performer portraying a character in a film; the term can apply to any gender.
actor.exampleUsage: The actor portrayed the main character.

actress.definition: A woman who performs a role in a film, play, or television show.
actress.exampleUsage: The actress portrayed the supporting character.

scene.definition: The place where some action occurs.
scene.exampleUsage: The scene takes place in a station.

soundtrack.definition: The music and recorded sounds accompanying a film.
soundtrack.exampleUsage: The soundtrack includes the film's recorded music and sound.

subtitle.definition: Text on screen showing spoken words or translations.
subtitle.exampleUsage: The subtitle displays the translated dialogue.

animation.definition: The creation of apparent movement through a sequence of designed images.
animation.exampleUsage: The animation creates apparent movement through designed images.

comedy.definition: A film genre using humor; a happy ending is not required in every example.
comedy.exampleUsage: The comedy uses humor in its story.

drama.definition: A film about serious situations and relationships.
drama.exampleUsage: The drama examines a serious relationship.

action.definition: A film genre emphasizing physical events, movement and excitement.
action.exampleUsage: The action film emphasizes physical events and movement.

horror.definition: A type of film intended to frighten viewers.
horror.exampleUsage: The horror film aims to frighten its audience.

romance.definition: A film centered on a romantic relationship.
romance.exampleUsage: The romance centers on a romantic relationship.

thriller.definition: A suspenseful adventure story or play or movie.
thriller.exampleUsage: The thriller builds suspense around the unresolved event.

documentary.definition: A film presenting information about real people, events, or subjects.
documentary.exampleUsage: The documentary presents a factual subject.

fantasy.definition: Fiction with a large amount of imagination in it.
fantasy.exampleUsage: The fantasy depicts an imagined world with supernatural elements.

science-fiction.definition: A genre of stories about imagined science, technology, space, future societies, or other speculative ideas.
science-fiction.exampleUsage: The science-fiction film explores imagined technology.

musical.definition: A film in which songs are part of the story.
musical.exampleUsage: The musical includes songs within its story.

ticket.definition: A printed or digital authorization for admission under cinema terms.
ticket.exampleUsage: The ticket provides admission under the venue's terms.

showtime.definition: The time at which something is supposed to begin.
showtime.exampleUsage: The showtime gives the scheduled start of the screening.

premiere.definition: The first public performance of a play or movie.
premiere.exampleUsage: The premiere is the film's first official public showing.

poster.definition: A large printed sheet fixed flat against a wall for decoration.
poster.exampleUsage: The poster promotes the film in the lobby.

marquee.definition: A sign above a cinema entrance advertising films.
marquee.exampleUsage: The marquee above the entrance displays film information.

rating.definition: A classification showing which age groups a film is suitable for.
rating.exampleUsage: The rating classifies the film under the relevant system.

review.definition: An article that evaluates a book, film, product, or event.
review.exampleUsage: The review evaluates the film's strengths and weaknesses.

audience.definition: A gathering of spectators or listeners at a (usually public) performance.

applause.definition: A demonstration of approval by clapping the hands together.

intermission.definition: The act of suspending activity temporarily.
intermission.exampleUsage: The intermission provides a scheduled break where the presentation includes one.
